references.text: Isaac asks Esau to hunt game and prepare food for him, which reflects his love for Esau because of the wild meat he enjoyed eating.
Rebekah helps Jacob deceive Isaac to receive the blessing, showing her strong love for and favoritism toward Jacob.
Malachi conveys the Lord's words: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated", which mirrors the parents' favoritism and God's sovereign election.
Paul quotes Malachi regarding God's love for Jacob and hatred of Esau to demonstrate God's sovereign choice, which can be related to the parents' different attitudes toward their two sons.
Malachi confirms God's eternal choice, which stands in contrast to Isaac's arbitrary love.
